questions.q: The radius of the second Bohr orbit, in terms of the Bohr radius, ${a}_{0},$ in ${Li}^{2 +}$ is:
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Radius of Bohr's orbit is given as,

$r = \dfrac{{a}_{0}n^{2}}{Z}$

n = orbit number

Z = atomic number

For ${2}^{nd}$ Bohr's orbit of ${\text{Li}}^{\text{2+}}$

${Li}^{2 +}, r = \dfrac{{a}_{0}\left(2\right)2}{3} = \dfrac{4{a}_{0}}{3}$

questions.q:
For hydrogen atom, the orbital/s with lowest energy is/are :
(A) 4 s
(B) $3 \mathrm{p}_x$
(C) $3 \mathrm{~d}_{x^2-y^2}$
(D) $3 \mathrm{~d}_{z^2}$
(E) $4 \mathrm{p}_z$ Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
For hydrogen atom and one electron species, the energy of orbitals is decided by the value of principal quantum number. Higher the value of principal quantum number, higher will be the energy of orbital.
$\therefore \quad(B),(C)$ and (D) have orbitals with the lowest energy.

questions.q: The shortest wavelength of hydrogen atom in Lyman series is $\lambda$. The longest wavelength in Balmer series of ${He}^{+}$ is
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
For Hydrogen atom ($H$) ($Z = 1$)~:~ \left(\dfrac{1}{λ}\right)H = {R}_{H} \times {1}^{2}\left[\dfrac{1}{12} - \dfrac{1}{\infty 2}\right]$~...(1)

For~${He}^{+}$~atom ($Z = 2$) :~\left(\dfrac{1}{λ}\right){He}^{+} = {R}_{H} \times {2}^{2} \times \left[\dfrac{1}{22} - \dfrac{1}{32}\right] = {R}_{H} \left[1 - \dfrac{4}{9}\right] = {R}_{H}\left(\dfrac{5}{9}\right)~..(2)

From (1) & (2)

\dfrac{\lambda{He}^{+}}{\lambdaH} = \dfrac{9}{5}

$\lambda{He}^{+} = \lambda $\times \dfrac{9}{5}

$\lambda{He}^{+} = $\dfrac{9\lambda}{5}.

$

questions.solution:
According to the de-Broglie hypothesis according to which all matters have both particle and wave nature. where $h =$ plank's constant, $p =$momentum, $\lambda =$ wavelength of particle. This type of graph is called a rectangular hyperbola. As $\lambda ∝ \dfrac{1}{p}$ we will have a rectangular hyperbola.

$\lambda = \dfrac{h}{p} \left[\lambda$∝ $\dfrac{1}{p}\right]

$⇒ \lambdap = h$ (constant)

So, the plot is a rectangular hyperbola.

$

Henry Moseley studied characteristic $X$-ray spectra of elements. The graph which represents his observation correctly is
Given $v =$~Frequency of X-ray emitted
~ ~ ~ ~ ~$Z =$ Atomic number
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Moseley's observation on characteristic $X$-ray spectra of elements relates frequency $( v )$ of $X$-rays emitted to the atomic number by the following relation:
$\sqrt{v} = a ( Z - b )$
The plot of $\sqrt{v}$ vs $Z$ is linear.

Based on this observation, the periodic law defined as the physical and chemical properties of the elements are periodic functions of their atomic numbers.

questions.q:
According to Bohr's atomic theory:
(A) Kinetic energy of electron is $∝ \dfrac{Z2}{n2} .$
(B) The product of velocity (v) of electron and principal quantum number \left(n\right), ' vn ' ∝ Z^{2} .$
(C) Frequency of revolution of electron in an orbit is $∝ \dfrac{Z3}{n3} .$
(D) Coulombic force of attraction on the electron is $∝ \dfrac{Z3}{n4} .$

Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

$
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
According to the Bohr's atomic theory, the kinetic energy of an electron is directly proportional to the square of the atomic number and inversely proportional to the square of the principal quantum number.&

(A)& $KE = 13 . 6\dfrac{z2}{n2}\dfrac{eV}{atom} ⇒ KE \alpha\dfrac{z2}{n2}$

(B) speed of~$e^{-}\alpha\dfrac{z}{n}$

$∴ v \times n \alpha z$

(C)~Frequency of revolution of~$e^{-} = \dfrac{v}{2\pi r}$

$∴$~Frequency~$\alpha\dfrac{z2}{n3}$

(D)~Coulombic force of attraction on the electron is directly proportional to the square of the atomic number and inversely proportional to the fourth power of the principal quantum number.~

~$F = \dfrac{{kq}_{1}{q}_{2}}{r2} = \dfrac{kze2}{r2} \left\{r $\alpha\dfrac{n2}{z}\right

$⇒ F $\alpha\dfrac{z}{\left(\dfrac{n2}{z}\right)2}

$⇒ F \alpha\dfrac{z3}{n4}$

$

questions.q:
Given below are two statements :
Statement (I) : It is impossible to specify simultaneously with arbitrary precision, both the linear momentum and the position of a particle.
Statement (II) : If the uncertainty in the measurement of position and uncertainty in measurement of momentum are equal for an electron, then the uncertainty in the measurement of velocity is $\geqslant \sqrt{\frac{\mathrm{h}}{\pi}} \times \frac{1}{2 \mathrm{~m}}$.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
According to Heisenberg's uncertainty principle, it is impossible to determine simultaneously the exact position and momentum of particle like electron
If $\begin{aligned} & \Delta p=\Delta x \\ & \Delta p \cdot \Delta x \geq \frac{h}{4 \pi} \\ &(\Delta p)^2 \geq \frac{h}{4 \pi} \\ & \Delta p \geq \sqrt{\frac{h}{\pi}} \times \frac{1}{2} \\ & m \Delta v \geq \sqrt{\frac{h}{\pi}} \times \frac{1}{2} \\ & \Delta v \geq \sqrt{\frac{h}{\pi}} \times \frac{1}{2 m}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Consider an imaginary ion $X 3 - 2248$.~The nucleus contains '$a$'$%$~more neutrons than the number of electrons in the ion. The value of '$a$' is
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
${X 2248}^{3 -}$

In an atomic representation~$X ZA$

Z is atomic number = 22

A is atomic mass number = 48.

No. of protons~$= Z = 22$

No. of neutrons~$= A - Z = 48 - 22 = 26$

No. of electrons~$= P - charge = 22 + 3 = 25$

$%$ of extra neutrons~than electrons~$= \dfrac{26 - 25}{25} \times 100 = 4 % = a %$

So, the value of a=4.

questions.q:
The electron in the& $n^{th}$ orbit of ${Li}^{2 +}$~ is excited to $( n + 1 )$ orbit using the radiation of energy $1 . 47 \times {10}^{- 17}J$ (as shown in the diagram). The value of $n$ is ___________

Given :~${R}_{H} = 2 . 18 \times {10}^{- 18}J$
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
The difference energy between two energy levels is&

$∆ E = 2 . 18 \times {10}^{- 18}\left[1{n}_{1}^{2} - 1{n}_{2}^{2}\right]J$

$1 . 47 \times {10}^{- 17} = 2 . 18 \times {10}^{- 18} \times ( 9 ) \left(\dfrac{1}{( n{)}^{2}} - \dfrac{1}{( n + 1{)}^{2}}\right)

$0 . 749 = $\dfrac{1}{n2} - \dfrac{1}{( n + 1{)}^{2}}

$n = 1$

Hence, the transition is taking place between~$1\overset{}{→}2$, and it comes under Lymann series.

If we take~$0 . 749 ≃ 0 . 75 = \dfrac{3}{4}$

$

questions.q: A proton and a ${Li}^{3 +}$ nucleus are accelerated by the same potential. If ${λ}_{Li}$ and ${λ}_{p}$ denote the de Broglie wavelengths of ${Li}^{3 +}$ and proton respectively, then the value of $\dfrac{\lambdaLi}{\lambdap}$ is $x \times {10}^{- 1}$. The value of $x$ is~_____~(Rounded off to the nearest integer) [Mass of ${Li}^{3 +} = 8 . 3$& mass of proton]
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
$\lambda = \dfrac{h}{2mqV}$

$\dfrac{\lambdaLi}{\lambdap} = \sqrt{\dfrac{{m}_{p}\left(e\right)V}{{m}_{Li}\left(3e\right)\left(V\right)}}{m}_{Li} = 8 . 3{m}_{p}$

$\dfrac{\lambdaLi}{\lambdap} = \sqrt{\dfrac{1}{8 . 3 \times 3}} = \dfrac{1}{5} = 0 . 2 = 2 \times {10}^{- 1}$
